::: {#sol-reuse-features}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
frozen_accs = []
for draw in range(n_draws):
    x_few, y_few = draw_few(draw)
    net, params = new_head(train_all=False)
    _ = train(net, x_few, y_few, n_epochs=30, params=params)
    frozen_accs.append(accuracy(net, x_high_test, y_high_test))
frozen_acc = np.mean(frozen_accs)
print(np.round(frozen_accs, 3))
# The prose below says the reused layers help; stop the render if they do not.
assert frozen_acc > scratch_acc
```

`low_net` classifies `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$low_acc)` of the test images of the digits 0 to 4 correctly.
With its [convolutional layers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-convolutional-layer) kept fixed and a new last layer,
the network classifies `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$frozen_acc)` of the digits 5 to 9 correctly,
averaged over the `r py$n_draws` draws,
against `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$scratch_acc)` for the networks trained from random weights.
So it is more accurate,
by `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (py$frozen_acc - py$scratch_acc))` percentage points.
The new layer has only `r format(16 * 4 * 4 * 5 + 5, big.mark = ",")` [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) to fit to the 20 images.
The fixed layers find strokes that they learned from `r py$n_low` images,
and those strokes help tell the digits 5 to 9 apart too.

:::
